candidates.workingClaim: The Universal Postal Union was founded in 1874 by a treaty signed in which Swiss city? Answer: Bern. Proposed featured link on 10-09: universal-postal-union-founded-1874. Asks where the founding treaty was signed, not the date; Geneva is the tempting international-city distractor.

Kepler's Supernova, first seen in 1604, is the most recent supernova in our own galaxy to be seen with the naked eye. Answer: True. Proposed additional link on 10-09: keplers-supernova-first-sighted-1604. Explains why the 1604 sighting still matters; the 1987 supernova is the natural misconception.

In which country was the revolutionary Che Guevara born? Answer: Argentina. Proposed additional link on 10-09: che-guevara-executed-1967. Recognizable figure; asks about his origins rather than the circumstances of his death. Cuba and Bolivia are plausible because of his later career.

Before King Sejong introduced the Hangeul alphabet, Koreans mainly wrote using what? Answer: Chinese characters. Proposed additional link on 10-09: hangeul-proclaimed-1446. Explains why the new alphabet mattered; depends on the proposed supplementary event hangeul-proclaimed-1446.

Under the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which of these may a country NOT do? Answer: Claim the Moon as its own territory. Proposed additional link on 10-10: outer-space-treaty-enters-force-1967. Tests the treaty's best-known principle rather than its date; the three permitted activities are explicitly free under Article I.

Apollo 7, the first crewed Apollo mission, flew around the Moon. Answer: False. Proposed featured link on 10-11: apollo-7-launches-1968. Corrects a natural assumption about the first crewed Apollo flight without asking for crew names or dates.

The Second Vatican Council allowed Mass to be celebrated in local languages instead of only in which language? Answer: Latin. Proposed additional link on 10-11: second-vatican-council-opens-1962. The council's most widely felt change; Italian is a tempting distractor because of the Vatican's location.

The Mary Rose, raised from the seabed in 1982, was the warship of which English monarch? Answer: Henry VIII. Proposed additional link on 10-11: mary-rose-raised-1982. Connects the 1982 recovery to the Tudor king, a recognizable anchor. All four options are English monarchs.

Equatorial Guinea became independent in 1968 from which European country? Answer: Spain. Proposed featured link on 10-12: equatorial-guinea-independence-1968. Same accessible pattern as the published Malta question; all four were colonial powers in Africa.

Munich's first Oktoberfest, in 1810, celebrated what? Answer: A royal wedding. Proposed additional link on 10-12: first-oktoberfest-1810. A fun origin story; the harvest is the common assumption. The coronation distractor is separate from the wedding.

The Knights Templar were originally founded to do what? Answer: Protect Christian pilgrims to the Holy Land. Proposed additional link on 10-13: templars-arrested-in-france-1307. Asks why the order existed instead of the arrest details; the French-king distractor echoes the event without being correct.

Which U.S. president was the first to live in the White House? Answer: John Adams. Proposed additional link on 10-13: white-house-cornerstone-laid-1792. Classic misconception: Washington oversaw construction but the house was first occupied in 1800.

In 1884, an international conference chose the meridian through an observatory in which place as the standard for longitude? Answer: Greenwich. Proposed additional link on 10-13: prime-meridian-greenwich-1884. Depends on the proposed supplementary event prime-meridian-greenwich-1884. Washington (the host city) and Paris (France's rival meridian) are deliberate near-misses.

Which famous work of medieval textile art shows the Norman Conquest and the Battle of Hastings? Answer: The Bayeux Tapestry. Proposed featured link on 10-14: battle-of-hastings-1066. The best-known artwork tied to the battle; text-only, so no new image rights or delivery are needed. Distractors are other famous medieval tapestries.

In 1947, Chuck Yeager's Bell X-1 took off from a runway under its own power before breaking the sound barrier. Answer: False. Proposed additional link on 10-14: yeager-breaks-sound-barrier-1947. A surprising detail of how the record flight worked, rather than the speed figure.

Which U.S. president told the nation in October 1962 that Soviet missile sites had been found in Cuba? Answer: John F. Kennedy. Proposed additional link on 10-14: u2-photographs-missiles-in-cuba-1962. Anchors the reconnaissance flight in the crisis most players know; options are the four consecutive Cold War presidents.

Shenzhou 5 made China the third country to send a person into space on its own spacecraft. Which two countries did it first? Answer: The Soviet Union and the United States. Proposed featured link on 10-15: shenzhou-5-yang-liwei-2003. Places China's milestone in the global space race; each distractor pairs a real space power with a country that had not launched a person.

The Cassini mission carried the Huygens probe, which landed on which moon of Saturn? Answer: Titan. Proposed additional link on 10-15: cassini-launches-to-saturn-1997. The mission's headline achievement; all four options are moons of Saturn.

Under the Gregorian calendar, which of these years was NOT a leap year? Answer: 1900. Proposed additional link on 10-15: gregorian-calendar-takes-effect-1582. Tests the reform's lasting rule rather than the 1582 date or the pope's name.

Propose featured relation on 10-10 from unchanged published xinhai-revolution-qing-dynasty to wuchang-uprising-1911. Britannica regards the October 10 Wuchang mutiny as the formal beginning of the revolution that overthrew the Qing. The question asks which dynasty that revolution ended.

Propose featured relation on 10-10 from unchanged published identify-sun-yat-sen to wuchang-uprising-1911. Britannica: after the Wuchang rising Sun returned from abroad and was elected provisional president. The portrait identifies the revolution's best-known leader.

Propose additional relation on 10-10 from unchanged published order-pacific-independence-milestones to fiji-independence-1970. The ordering includes 'Fiji becomes independent' (1970), the event itself.

Propose additional relation on 10-12 from unchanged published order-americas-milestones to columbus-sights-land-1492. The ordering includes 'Columbus reaches the Caribbean' (1492), the landfall itself.

Propose additional relation on 10-12 from unchanged published columbian-exchange-meaning to columbus-sights-land-1492. The exchange named after Columbus began with the 1492 crossing; the question explains its consequences rather than the landfall.

Propose additional relation on 10-12 from unchanged published voskhod-1-multiperson-crew to voskhod-1-launches-1964. Exact match: the question asks which spacecraft first carried a multi-person crew. Hard; kept as published.

Propose featured relation on 10-12 from unchanged published order-african-independence-1960s to equatorial-guinea-independence-1968. The ordering includes 'Equatorial Guinea becomes independent' (October 12, 1968), the featured event.

Propose featured relation on 10-13 from unchanged published chile-miners-days-underground to chilean-miners-rescued-2010. Exact match on the rescue. The event summary states 69 days, so reading the story first reveals the answer; that is learning, not leakage in the quiz itself.

Propose additional relation on 10-14 from unchanged published identify-napoleon-bonaparte to battles-of-jena-auerstedt-1806. Britannica names Napoleon as the victor at Jena-Auerstedt. The 1812 portrait identifies him without depending on the battle.

Propose additional relation on 10-14 from unchanged published identify-martin-luther-king-jr to mlk-awarded-nobel-peace-prize-1964. The portrait's explanation already cites his 1964 Nobel Peace Prize. Depends on the proposed supplementary event.

Propose additional relation on 10-09 from unchanged published order-korean-cultural-printing-milestones to hangeul-proclaimed-1446. The ordering ends with 'Hunminjeongeum is published' (1446), the event itself. Depends on the proposed supplementary event.
